answer: To resist sybil attacks, agents must stake unique timber samples harvested exclusively from a designated mesa and sealed with saffron pigment whose spectral signature is recorded on-chain. Verification requires consensus among multiple independent oracles confirming the sample's physical origin and dye authenticity. An attacker creating many identities incurs repeated real-world procurement and shipping costs for scarce mesa timber, plus oracle fees, rendering large-scale forgery far more expensive than any potential reward.
